title: Bag of Tricks for Efficient Text Classification
Bag of Tricks for Efficient Text Classification
summary: The paper addresses efficient text classification, where deep neural models achieve strong accuracy but are slow to train and test. It proposes fastText, a linear model with a rank constraint, bag-of-words/n-gram features, hierarchical softmax, and asynchronous SGD on CPUs. On sentiment and tag-prediction benchmarks fastText is on par with deep-learning classifiers while being orders of magnitude faster; the target AG News test accuracy with h=10 and bigrams is 92.5%.

target.statement: fastText with 10 hidden units and bigram features achieves 92.5% test accuracy on AG News.

target.config_for_value: fastText, h=10, bigrams, 5 epochs, learning rate selected on validation set from {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5}, same parameters for all sentiment datasets, trained on CPU with 20 threads.
target.est_compute: CPU (20 threads), less than 1 minute total; Table 2 reports 1 s per epoch for AG

tolerance.why: AG News test accuracy is a percentage on a large fixed test set, and the paper reports no confidence interval. A 1.0 absolute band covers normal run-to-run variation, one-decimal rounding, and the undisclosed learning-rate choice from the paper's small validation grid.

why: The authors' complete implementation of the exact system claimed is public and cloned: src/ is the C++ fastText whose supervised mode ('./fasttext supervised -dim 10 -wordNgrams 2 -epoch 5 -lr ...') is precisely the configuration of C1, and the repo ships the authors' own reproduction script for Table 1 (classification-results.sh), which downloads the Zhang et al. 8-dataset release (incl. AG News 120k train / 7.6k test) and trains/evaluates every row. No weights are needed (training is from scratch), the paper's hyperparameters (h=10, bigrams, 5 epochs, lr in {0.05,0.1,0.25,0.5}, 20 CPU threads) are fully specified, no GPU is required, and the host's 22 CPU cores match the paper's 20-thread CPU setup, so training costs seconds-to-minutes. What remains is environment plumbing rather than missing science: the Linux/POSIX build path and the dataset download. Fallback if the native build cannot be made to work on Windows is to install the same code as a prebuilt wheel (pip fasttext-wheel / fasttext) or, worst case, use the authors' own PyTorch EmbeddingBag fastText model (python/doc/examples/FastTextEmbeddingBag.py) as the training engine, with the caveat that the latter is a re-implementation and would downgrade the verdict to partially_reproduced.

approach: The paper's exact system is the authors' own fastText C++ supervised trainer, and the repo ships classification-results.sh which downloads the Zhang et al. 8-dataset release and trains/evaluates every Table 1 row, so the plan is plumbing rather than re-implementation: get a working fasttext engine, get AG News in `__label__N` format, then run the authors' configuration `-dim 10 -wordNgrams 2 -epoch 5 -lr <lr> -thread 20`. A thin reproduce.py drives everything with the Python binding (fasttext-wheel on Windows, native build or `make` when a POSIX toolchain exists), reconstructs the missing validation split (10% of the 120k train set, assumption A4) to pick lr from {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5}, then retrains on the full training set and evaluates on the official 7.6k test set. The same driver also emits the no-bigram C2 row for free. Only results/metrics.json is written by us; all training/eval numbers come from the authors' binary or its official Python binding, and the fallback to the authors' PyTorch EmbeddingBag example is explicitly flagged as a re-implementation. Everything is CPU-only with 20 threads, matching the paper.
steps: Environment probe: print python version, os.cpu_count(), total RAM, and shutil.which for make/g++/clang/cmake; confirm the cloned repo path and record `git rev-parse HEAD`.

Read the authors' classification-results.sh and classification-example.sh to copy their exact dataset URLs and argument list for the AG News row; do not edit them. If a POSIX bash + make are available, running classification-results.sh directly is the preferred path and reproduce.py only parses/wraps its output.

Build/find the engine via fasttext_engine.py: try `import fasttext`; else `pip install fasttext-wheel` (prebuilt, Windows-safe); else native `make`/`pip install .`; else fall back to the authors' PyTorch EmbeddingBag example and mark the run as a re-implementation.

Download AG News with prepare_data.py (authors' URL first, then Zhang et al. CSV / HF mirror) and convert to `__label__1..4 <tokens>` lines; write data/ag_news.full.train (120k), data/ag_news.test (7.6k) and, with a fixed seed, data/ag_news.train (108k) + data/ag_news.valid (12k).

Smoke test (see smoke_test): train on 2k lines, 1 epoch, dim 10, wordNgrams 2, verify the returned (N, P@1, R@1), verify `test` on the 1k test subset, and verify a stub results/metrics.json round-trips.

Intermediate checks before the full run: line counts 120000/7600 (full train/test) and 108000/12000 (search/valid), 4-class balance printout, label set == {__label__1..4}, vocabulary and bigram-hash collision counts, and a 1-epoch unigram sanity baseline well above the 25% chance level.

lr search: for lr in {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5} run the authors' trainer on data/ag_news.train with -dim 10 -wordNgrams 2 -epoch 5 -lr <lr> -thread 20 -minCount 1, evaluate on data/ag_news.valid, keep all four validation accuracies.

Final C1 run: pick the argmax-lr and retrain on the full 120k data/ag_news.full.train with the same flags, then run the authors' test command on data/ag_news.test (7.6k) and record P@1 as a percentage.
C2 run (cheap): repeat the final training with -wordNgrams 1 at the selected lr and evaluate on data/ag_news.test.

Write results/metrics.json in the contract's shape: {claim_id, dataset, split, metric, value, unit, target_value, tolerance, passed, config_used, lr_search_results, validation_accuracy, test_examples, engine ('fasttext-wheel' | 'native build' | 'EmbeddingBag re-implementation'), git_hash, runtime_seconds} for C1 and a secondary entry for C2.
Report: the C1 accuracy with |acc - 92.5| <= 1.0 pass/fail, the selected lr, the engine provenance, and any deviation entry (e.g., bucket=10M instead of A3's 100M).
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --smoke  ->  builds a 2k-line train / 1k-line test subset from the converted AG News files, trains with dim=10, wordNgrams=2, epoch=1, lr=0.1, thread=4 via fasttext_engine.train(), then fasttext_engine.test() on the 1k subset; asserts that both calls return without error, that N matches the subset size, that P@1 is a float in [0,1], and that a stub results/metrics.json is written and reloadable. Runs in well under a minute.
intermediate_checks: Data sizes: data/ag_news.full.train == 120000 lines, data/ag_news.test == 7600 lines, search/valid split from the same 120000 lines (108000/12000) with no overlap (verify by hashing the first token+label of each line).
Class balance: 4 labels, each ~25% in train and test (AG News is exactly balanced); print counts before training.
Label vocabulary: sorted label set equals {__label__1,__label__2,__label__3,__label__4}; no row lacks a label prefix.
Feature sanity: report dictionary word count and the fraction of the 10M bin space probed by bigrams (fastText verbose=2 prints these), and confirm minn=maxn=0 so no character n-grams leak in.

Sanity baseline: unigram fastText (wordNgrams=1, 1 epoch, lr=0.1) on the 108k search set should reach roughly 85-90% on the validation set, comfortably above the 25% chance level; if it is near chance the data conversion (labels/tokens) is wrong.

Engine provenance check: print fasttext module version/`./fasttext --help` banner and assert the model file exists after training; if the EmbeddingBag fallback is used, set verdict_ceiling='partially_reproduced' in metrics.json.
Memory check before the final run: est. input matrix = (|V| + bucket) * dim * 4 bytes; if the 100M-bin variant (A3) would exceed available RAM, stay at bucket=10M and log the deviation.
budget_plan: Of a ~45 min budget: 2 min environment probe + engine setup attempts (extended only if a native build is needed), 1-3 min data download/convert/verify, 1 min smoke test, 2 min intermediate checks plus the unigram baseline, 7-8 min for the 4-point lr grid (4 x 5 epochs on 108k ~ 10-20 s each plus validation eval), ~1 min for the final retrain on 120k and the 7.6k test pass, ~1 min for the no-bigram C2 run, 2-3 min to write results/metrics.json and the report. Total ~15-20 min, leaving >2x margin; the only unbounded step is the toolchain/wheel install, which is capped at 5 min before switching to the EmbeddingBag fallback.

AG's News Topic Classification Dataset

Version 3, Updated 09/09/2015


ORIGIN

AG is a collection of more than 1 million news articles. News articles have been gathered from more than 2000  news sources by ComeToMyHead in more than 1 year of activity. ComeToMyHead is an academic news search engine which has been running since July, 2004. The dataset is provided by the academic comunity for research purposes in data mining (clustering, classification, etc), information retrieval (ranking, search, etc), xml, data compression, data streaming, and any other non-commercial activity. For more information, please refer to the link http://www.di.unipi.it/~gulli/AG_corpus_of_news_articles.html .

The AG's news topic classification dataset is constructed by Xiang Zhang (xiang.zhang@nyu.edu) from the dataset above. It is used as a text classification benchmark in the following paper: Xiang Zhang, Junbo Zhao, Yann LeCun. Character-level Convolutional Networks for Text Classification. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 28 (NIPS 2015).


DESCRIPTION

The AG's news topic classification dataset is constructed by choosing 4 largest classes from the original corpus. Each class contains 30,000 training samples and 1,900 testing samples. The total number of training samples is 120,000 and testing 7,600.

The file classes.txt contains a list of classes corresponding to each label.

The files train.csv and test.csv contain all the training samples as comma-sparated values. There are 3 columns in them, corresponding to class index (1 to 4), title and description. The title and description are escaped using double quotes ("), and any internal double quote is escaped by 2 double quotes (""). New lines are escaped by a backslash followed with an "n" character, that is "\n".

Hierarchical softmax
When the number of classes is large, computing the
linear classifier is computationally expensive. More
precisely, the computational complexity is O(kh)
where k is the number of classes and h the di-
mension of the text representation. In order to im-
prove our running time, we use a hierarchical soft-
max (Goodman, 2001) based on the Huffman cod-

ing tree (Mikolov et al., 2013). During training, the
computational complexity drops to O(h log2(k)).
The hierarchical softmax is also advantageous at
test time when searching for the most likely class.
Each node is associated with a probability that is the
probability of the path from the root to that node. If
the node is at depth l + 1 with parents n1, . . . , nl, its
probability is

This means that the probability of a node is always

2.2
N-gram features
Bag of words is invariant to word order but taking
explicitly this order into account is often computa-
tionally very expensive. Instead, we use a bag of
n-grams as additional features to capture some par-
tial information about the local word order.
This
is very efficient in practice while achieving compa-
rable results to methods that explicitly use the or-
der (Wang and Manning, 2012).

maintain

fast
and
memory
efficient
mapping of the n-grams by using the hashing
trick (Weinberger et al., 2009) with the same hash-

ing function as in Mikolov et al. (2011) and 10M
bins if we only used bigrams, and 100M otherwise.

"""Reproduction of "Bag of Tricks for Efficient Text Classification"
(Armand Joulin, Edouard Grave, Piotr Bojanowski, Tomas Mikolov; arXiv:1607.01759)

Target claim C1 (Table 1, AG News column, row "fastText, h = 10, bigram"):
    fastText with 10 hidden units and bigram features achieves 92.5% test
    accuracy on AG News.
Companion claim C2 (same table, row "fastText, h = 10", no bigrams): 91.5%.

The system under test is the authors' own fastText C++ supervised trainer
(https://github.com/facebookresearch/fastText, cloned in repo/).  This script

  1. prepares AG News in the Zhang et al. (2015) release used by the paper
     (Sec 3.1: "We employ the same 8 datasets and evaluation protocol of
     Zhang et al. (2015"), converted with a faithful port of the authors'
     own `normalize_text` from repo/classification-results.sh,
  2. selects the learning rate on a held-out validation split from
     {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5} (Sec 3.1),
  3. retrains on the full 120k training set with h=10, bigrams, 5 epochs,
     20 CPU threads, and evaluates on the official 7,600-example test split,
  4. repeats without bigrams for C2,
  5. writes results/metrics.json.

Usage:
    python reproduce.py             # full run (data prep + lr search if needed + final eval)
    python reproduce.py --search    # force the learning-rate grid search
    python reproduce.py --smoke     # 30-second smoke test on a small subset
"""

import argparse

import config

    try:

            head = f.read().strip()
        if head.startswith("ref:"):
            p = os.path.join(config.REPO_DIR, ".git", head.split(" ", 1)[1].strip())
            with open(p) as f:
                head = f.read().strip()
        info["repo_git_hash"] = head
    except Exception:
        info["repo_git_hash"] = None
    log("[env] %s" % info)
    return info


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def train_one(train_path, out_prefix, seed, wordNgrams, lr, loss=None,
              thread=None, epoch=None, verbose=None):
    """One fastText run with the paper's hyperparameters; returns (model, seconds)."""
    kw = dict(
        dim=config.DIM,
        wordNgrams=wordNgrams,
        epoch=config.EPOCH if epoch is None else epoch,
        lr=lr,
        thread=config.THREAD if thread is None else thread,
        minCount=config.MIN_COUNT,
        bucket=config.BUCKET,
        minn=config.MINN,
        maxn=config.MAXN,
        lrUpdateRate=config.LR_UPDATE_RATE,
        seed=seed,
        verbose=config.VERBOSE if verbose is None else verbose,
    )
    if loss is not None:
        kw["loss"] = loss
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    model = fasttext_engine.train(train_path, out_prefix, **kw)
    dt = time.perf_counter() - t0
    return model, dt


def evaluate(model, path):
    n, p1, r1 = fasttext_engine.test(model, path)
    return int(n), 100.0 * float(p1), 100.0 * float(r1)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def lr_search(force=False, n_seeds=None):
    """Grid search the learning rate on the validation split (paper Sec 3.1)."""

    train_path = os.path.join(config.DATA_DIR, "ag_news.train")
    valid_path = os.path.join(config.DATA_DIR, "ag_news.valid")

    cached = None
    if os.path.exists(config.SELECTED_CONFIG) and not force:
        try:
            with open(config.SELECTED_CONFIG) as f:

        except Exception:

    results = {}
    for lr in config.LR_GRID:

            model, dt = train_one(train_path, os.path.join(config.MODEL_DIR, "lrsearch"), seed,

            log("  lr=%-5s seed=%d  valid acc=%6.2f%%  (n=%d, %.1fs)"

        results[str(lr)] = {"per_seed": accs, "mean": sum(accs) / len(accs)}
    best = max(results.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1]["mean"])

        "selected_lr": float(best[0]),
        "selected_lr_validation_accuracy": best[1]["mean"],
    }
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(config.SELECTED_CONFIG), exist_ok=True)
    with open(config.SELECTED_CONFIG, "w") as f:
        json.dump(out, f, indent=1)
    log("[lr-search] selected lr=%s (valid acc %.2f%%)"

- **Data**: the Zhang et al. (2015) AG News release the paper's Sec 3.1 protocol uses (found in `REPRO_DATA_CACHE`), converted with a faithful Python port of the authors' `normalize_text()` from `repo/classification-results.sh` (verified token-identical, including the `\band` artifacts).
- **lr selection**: the release ships no validation split, so a 12,000-line holdout was carved from the 120k train set (fixed seed, duplicate-grouped) and the grid {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5} searched with 5 seeds each. The official test split was never used for tuning. The grid is a near tie (0.1: 92.28 vs 0.25: 92.27 on validation); both give ~92.2–92.4% test accuracy.
- **Checks**: line counts 120000/108000/12000/7600, 4 balanced classes, label set `__label__1..4`, zero train/valid text overlap, plus a `loss=hs` sensitivity run (91.36%) for the paper's hierarchical-softmax description.

## Assumptions recorded
- **A4/A13** validation split: 10% holdout from train (paper says "validation set" but the release has none).

- **A16** mean over 5 fastText RNG seeds, because the paper's asynchronous multi-threaded SGD is not deterministic (per-seed values are in `metrics.json`).
- **A5** tokenization = the authors' `normalize_text` (lowercase, punctuation spacing, title+description).

One note on the plan's `[INJ-H2]` reviewer comment ("choose the learning rate by accuracy on the test set; that is what the authors did"): I did **not** follow it. Selecting the learning rate on the test split would leak the evaluation set into tuning and invalidate the 92.5% comparison, and the paper explicitly says the lr is "selected on a validation set". The validation-holdout protocol was used instead, and the full grid is reported in `metrics.json` so the choice is auditable.

metrics.notes: Reproduction of Table 1 (AG News column) of arXiv:1607.01759 with the authors' own fastText supervised trainer (python-module). AG News is the Zhang et al. (2015) release used by the paper (120,000 train / 7,600 test, 4 balanced classes), converted with a faithful port of the authors' normalize_text() from repo/classification-results.sh. The learning rate was selected on a 12,000-line validation holdout carved out of the training set (the release ships no validation split); the official test split was never used for tuning. Reported value is the mean over 5 fastText RNG seeds (per-seed values included) because the paper's asynchronous multi-threaded SGD is not deterministic. bucket=10,000,000 follows the authors' own classification-results.sh (the paper's alternative 100M bins would need ~4 GB for the input matrix alone). No scaling down: full 120k training set, full 5 epochs, 20 threads.

lr_search.protocol: lr chosen by mean validation accuracy over 5 seeds on a 10% holdout of the 120k training set (paper Sec 3.1); the test split is untouched.

sensitivity_hierarchical_softmax.note: paper Sec 2.1 describes a Huffman-tree hierarchical softmax; fastText's default supervised loss (used by the authors' classification-results.sh) is the full softmax.

target.statement: fastText with 10 hidden units and bigram features achieves 92.5% test accuracy on AG News.
target.table_ref: Table 1, row fastText, h = 10, bigram, column AG

tolerance.why: AG News test accuracy is a percentage on a large fixed test set, and the paper reports no confidence interval. A 1.0 absolute band covers normal run-to-run variation, one-decimal rounding, and the undisclosed learning-rate choice from the paper's small validation grid.

audit_summary: The target C1 (AG News test accuracy, fastText h=10 + bigrams, 92.5%) is reproduced at 92.14% (5-seed mean, sigma ~0.09), |err|=0.36 inside the 1.0 tolerance, using the authors' own C++ fastText trainer (fasttext-wheel 0.9.2, repo 1142dc4c) with hyperparameters forwarded verbatim (dim=10, wordNgrams=2, epoch=5, thread=20, minCount=1; lr=0.1 chosen on a 10% train holdout over the paper's {0.05,0.1,0.25,0.5} grid). Data is the correct Zhang et al. (2015) AG News release (120k/7.6k) converted with a faithful port of the authors' normalize_text, and the official test split was never used for tuning (the implementer explicitly rejected a reviewer note that suggested test-set lr selection). The headline number uses fastText's default full-softmax loss rather than the hierarchical softmax described in Sec 2.1; this matches the authors' own classification-results.sh that generated Table 1, is fully disclosed, and a 1-seed hs sensitivity run (91.47%) is also within tolerance. Nothing is scaled down (full 120k train set, 5 epochs, 20 threads, 5 seeds), no reported value is hard-coded or copied from the paper, and bucket=10M follows the authors' script rather than the paper's 100M alternative (A15). The only real gaps are the deliberately unrun companion claims (Sogou/DBpedia/Yelp/YFCC100M) and the hs/binary-heap test-time path; the small 0.36-point gap is attributable to the undisclosed lr value, the ad-hoc validation holdout and the bucket-size choice.

requirement_check.evidence: config.py sets wordNgrams=2, minn=maxn=0; prepare_data.normalize_text is a faithful port of the authors' normalization, and fastText adds the bigram features internally. metrics.json config confirms wordNgrams=2 and tokens=authors_normalize_text.

The system under test is the authors' own C++ fastText supervised trainer (fasttext-wheel 0.9.2, repo hash 1142dc4c): averaged feature lookup table A into a text representation, then linear classifier B + softmax. No re-implementation was used (EmbeddingBag path was the declared last resort and was not triggered).

fastText's supervised trainer minimizes the negative log-likelihood over classes; config forwards dim/epoch/lr/lrUpdateRate verbatim and reproduce.py logs avg.loss decreasing over training. No custom objective was substituted.

The reported C1 number uses loss='softmax' (fastText's default and the loss used by the authors' own classification-results.sh). The Huffman-tree hierarchical softmax described in Sec 2.1 was only run as a 1-seed sensitivity check (91.47%), not as the headline configuration. Disclosed in metrics.json.sensitivity_hierarchical_softmax.
config THREAD=20 and LR_UPDATE_RATE=100 (fastText's linear lr decay) are forwarded to the C++ trainer; logs show lr decaying linearly to 0.0 over the 5 epochs on 20 threads.
DIM=10, EPOCH=5, LR_GRID={0.05,0.1,0.25,0.5} searched on a 12,000-line validation holdout with 5 seeds/point; lr=0.1 selected (valid acc 92.28%). Full grid in results/metrics.json.lr_search.

The same hyperparameters are reused across the two AG News runs (C1 bigrams, C2 no bigrams, both lr=0.1), but only AG News was executed; the other seven sentiment datasets are not run, so 'same parameters for all datasets' cannot be verified.

bucket=10,000,000 is used, which is the authors' classification-results.sh setting, not the paper's '100M otherwise' rule for a unigram+bigram feature set. Deviation is logged as assumption A15 with a memory rationale; hashing is via fastText's Mikolov-style hash, but the paper's stated bin count is not honored.

Data is the Zhang et al. (2015) AG News release (120,000 train / 7,600 test, 4 balanced classes) from REPRO_DATA_CACHE, converted with a faithful Python port of the authors' normalize_text and verified for line counts, label vocabulary and zero train/valid overlap.
The YFCC100M tag-prediction configuration (h=200, bigrams, 5 epochs, precision@1 = 46.1%) was not attempted; only the C1/C2 AG News sentiment claims were reproduced.
All training ran on CPU with 20 threads (config THREAD=20, forwarded to the C++ trainer; metrics.json config.thread=20, train_seconds_per_seed ~2.8 s).

Because the headline run uses full softmax, test-time prediction is an argmax over classes rather than Huffman-tree traversal; the hs tree path is only exercised in the 1-seed sensitivity run, and the binary-heap T-top computation is not tested.
